definition: Having two pixel states: on and off.
example: One bit can represent one monochrome pixel.

definition: A base-2 way to write values using only `0` and `1`.
A bit's numbered place in a byte, counting from 0 on the right.
Reverse each bit of an integer. Python integers are not restricted to eight positions.
A bit pattern used to select or change chosen bit positions.
Combines bits so a result bit is `1` only when both inputs have `1`.
Combines bits so a `1` in either input produces a `1`; useful for setting a bit.
Moves a bit pattern left or right. For nonnegative integers, left shifts add zeroes on the right; right shifts discard the lowest positions.
A group of four bits, or half a byte.
A base-16 notation that writes each group of four bits as one digit.
A way of writing or arranging a value.
example: `60`, `0x3C`, and `0b00111100` write the same value in different bases.

definition: A way to represent color with red, green, and blue components. In this lesson, each component gets one byte.
One component of a color, such as red. Its byte value selects how much of that component to contribute.
example: In `#0000FF`, the blue channel is 255 and the other two are zero.

definition: Putting several values into separate bit positions of one larger integer.
example: In our packed RGB value, red occupies bits 16 through 23.
